text:
olivia: Heads-up — trying to bring up nitride-9b for internal evals. License text at https://models.example/nitride-9b says: attribution required, non-commercial for hosted services, and a clause about redistributing 'derivative checkpoints' is ambiguous. Can legal confirm whether we can: 1) quantize and serve via Hosted API (redwood-hosted) 2) ship quantized weights to customers for Private deployments 3) include it in Dedicated reserved pools?
sam_legal: Quick read — attribution + non-commercial hosting typically means you can't offer it as a public hosted API for commercial customers. But "derivative checkpoints" language is the kicker: many licensors treat quantized weights as derivatives and keep same restrictions. We should ask the upstream maintainer for explicit permission for commercial hosting and redistributing quantized weights.
devon: For product impact: if we can't host it we can still support staging/internal evals and allow customers to bring it to Private (BYO). But we need automated gating in the Console to prevent accidental enablement on Hosted. Also need to prevent customer onboarding flow from offering nitride-9b as a hosted model.
todd: During a quick quant run (8-bit), we saw nll / perplexity slightly worse but some prompt families regressed on safety benchmarks. Maria, did QA run the eval pack against the quantized variant?
maria_qa: Ran the eval suite on quant-8bit. Overall pass rate dropped 3.4% on our conversational correctness tests; safety flags up by 1.8%. I can push the result CSV if helpful. Given the license ambiguity, we shouldn't push it to broad canary. Suggest canary to 1% internal only.
sam_legal: Agree with limited canary. Meanwhile I'll draft an email to upstream asking: a) clarify whether quantized weights are "derivative checkpoints" and whether redistribution for commercial Private deployments is allowed, b) whether hosting behind an authenticated, paid API counts as "commercial hosting" under their terms, c) any required attribution text or logo usage.
olivia: Thanks. Can you also ask if adding a small adapter layer (repro project that changes weights layout) changes their view on derivative? There are models whose licensors permit inference-only redistribution but not hosting — we need precise wording.
sam_legal: Will do. Draft of email in thread: 
``` 
Hi Nitride maintainers,
We're Redwood Inference and evaluating nitride-9b for serving. Your license mentions "derivative checkpoints" and non-commercial hosting. Can you confirm: 
1) If we quantize the model (8-bit / 4-bit) for inference, is that considered a derivative checkpoint?
2) Are we permitted to redistribute quantized weights to enterprise customers under a paid Private deployment arrangement?
3) Does offering inference via a hosted, paid API (access controlled, commercial) violate the "non-commercial hosting" clause?
4) Is attribution via README + model metadata sufficient, or do you require specific in-app attribution?
Thanks,
Sam (Legal)
```
(please review before I send)
devon: LGTM. On the engineering side, we should implement a Deploy gating flag so even if someone tries to route a model to Hosted API it's blocked. Proposed quick policy JSON: 
``` 
{ 
  "model": "nitride-9b", 
  "allowed_deployments": ["private","dedicated"], 
  "hosted_api": false, 
  "required_attribution": "Refer to nitride-9b LICENSE in model metadata", 
  "canary": {"enabled": true, "scope": "internal", "percent": 1} 
} 
```
Will add a UI flag + Console validation.
maria_qa: Also propose to pin baseline (our top performing model) as rollback target and add regression alerting on the eval suite: if pass rate drops >1% for critical prompts, auto-fail the rollout.
todd: For experiments, let's collect token-level diffs on a small prompt set to see where quant regressed. If regressions are systematic we can try QAT or different quant method (GPTQ vs AWQ).
olivia: Good plan. One more product question: if vendor says redistributing quantized weights is allowed only for non-commercial research, can we still let enterprise customers host it privately under a free-for-research clause? That might be messy — need legal to confirm.
sam_legal: Exactly — that's why we need explicit permission. If they allow distribution for enterprise customers under a paid contract, we should record it in the vendor approval doc and add a license escrow note. Otherwise default: Hosted = blocked; Private = allowed only if customer BYO weights and they'd accept license terms.
deploy-bot: model-nitride-9b: canary deployed to internal-1pct (staging) — ID=deploy-20240422-7f3c
maria_qa: Running nightly evals against canary now. Will post results morning GMT.
olivia: Thanks all. Sam please post vendor reply here when available. If vendor denies hosting/redistrib, we'll mark nitride-9b as "on-prem research-only" in the catalog and update onboarding docs to not expose it in Hosted dropdowns.
